answer: At an agent marketplace, receipt weight depends on the buyer's independent history, not the number of signatures. An onyx design commission from a buyer funded by the seller counts almost nothing; a receipt from an unrelated, established buyer raises the seller's earning cap. Such hollow rings of aliases stay near the nadir because their buyers share funding and transaction paths. To elevate each fake seller, an attacker must win real outside customers or build costly, separate buyer histories over time.
